definitions.explanation: A period of silence observed to honor the dead or show respect, typically with eyes closed and head bowed. Common at memorial ceremonies and commemorative events.

examples.japanese: {黙祷|もくとう}を{捧|ささ}げる。
examples.english: Offer a moment of silent prayer.

examples.japanese: {犠牲者|ぎせいしゃ}のために{一分間|いっぷんかん}の{黙祷|もくとう}が{行|おこな}われた。
examples.english: A one-minute moment of silence was held for the victims.

examples.japanese: {式典|しきてん}は{全員|ぜんいん}の{黙祷|もくとう}で{始|はじ}まり、{静|しず}かに{亡|な}くなった{方々|かたがた}を{偲|しの}んだ。
examples.english: The ceremony began with a moment of silence by all attendees, quietly remembering those who had passed away.

notes:
USAGE:
A compound of {黙|もく} (silence) and {祷|とう} (prayer). Used as both a noun and a suru verb ({黙祷|もくとう}する). At Japanese memorial services, the emcee typically announces {黙祷|もくとう} to signal the start and {黙祷|もくとう}やめ or お{直|なお}りください to signal the end.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {黙祷|もくとう}を{捧|ささ}げる (to offer a moment of silence)
- {黙祷|もくとう}する (to observe a moment of silence)
- {一分間|いっぷんかん}の{黙祷|もくとう} (a one-minute moment of silence)
- {黙祷|もくとう}！ (Silence! — announcement at ceremonies)
